title: Battle Dice class evolution: vocation catalog v0.2 (specification only; the game does not load it)

baseline.description: The shipped rules and content this catalog was written against. The validator compares both.

rank_thresholds_by_group.description: Cumulative mastery points needed for ranks 1..rank_count.

threat_min_by_group_and_rank.description: Entry r-1 is the lowest encounter threat that still awards mastery to a hero at rank r. The last entry is unused: a mastered vocation earns nothing.

stat_caps.description: Most a hero can ever gain per stat from all mastery rewards together.

face_library.description: New faces only. A die may also use any face of the shipped dice.json by its id.

engine_support.description: existing: rules 1.1.1 already implement this. new: the engine must change first; an engine_gaps entry says how.

face.description: Exactly the shipped die-face shape (dice.json face_library), so a face can be moved into the game unchanged.

die.description: The shipped die shape. affinity_class is the id of the new vocation that owns the die.

faces.description: Face ids from this catalog's face_library or the shipped dice.json. The validator requires exactly `size` of them.

tags_any.description: When present, the face must carry at least one of these tags.

schedule.description: Slot model. A plan of one action is always legal. A plan of two or more actions needs max_actions or fewer actions, each fitting its own slot. With order 'slots' it must fill every slot and resolves in slot order. With order 'action_speed' it may use any of the slots and resolves by descending action speed, the player's order breaking ties. len(slots) equals max_actions. The shipped policies map to: single = one slot of every category; sequence = two slots, one category in the first; free = max_actions slots of every category, order 'action_speed', distinct_categories false.

distinct_categories.description: No two actions of one plan may share a category.

passive.description: A typed passive. The three shipped types keep the shipped fields; every other type is new to the engine.

attack_tag_invariant.description: A content invariant, not an engine filter: every Attack face the vocation can roll (its dice and its upgrade family's reforge and imbue faces) must carry this tag. The validator enforces it.

reaction.description: The shipped reaction shape plus id and engine_support. Only reactions that differ from every shipped one are listed.

skill.description: A learned skill. Which vocation teaches it, and at which rank, is stated once, in that vocation's skills_learned.

encounter.description: A mastery-eligible encounter. 'shipped' is one of the two battles in the shipped encounters.json; 'to_author' needs an enemy line-up the game does not have yet and cannot be used for training until it does.

engine_gap.description: Something v0.1 asks for that rules 1.1.1 cannot express. used_by entries are '<kind>:<id>'.

prerequisite.description: Boolean expression over one hero's progress. 'mastered' means the last rank of that vocation. Route ids: the alternatives of a top-level 'any' are route_0, route_1, ... in this order; any other prerequisite is the single route route_0. Alternatives may be appended, never reordered or removed.

novice_vocation.description: A shipped class. Its name, stats, dice, schedule, passive and reaction are read from the shipped classes.json through class_id and must not be repeated here.

mastery_rewards.description: Granted once, on mastery (the last rank). Empty: the skill is the reward.

new_vocation.description: A vocation the game does not have yet, written in the shipped class vocabulary.

reaction_id.description: A reaction of this catalog or of the shipped classes.json.

upgrade_family.description: The shipped class whose reforge and imbue tables this vocation uses.

mastery_rewards.description: Granted once, on mastery (the last rank). Empty: the skill is the reward.
